summary: Replaced the legacy app_code-scoped RBAC system with a shared, single-app 'accessrbac' core used identically by myidsan and myseliasan. The new core stores roles (access_role) and a per-endpoint permission matrix (access_role_permission) in each app's own database, with no app_code dimension. A superadmin role flag bypasses the matrix entirely; all other roles are governed by longest-prefix path matching per HTTP verb. Built-in 'superadmin' and 'viewer' roles are seeded on startup. The shared management surface is GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/access-rbac/roles and GET/POST/DELETE /api/access-rbac/permissions (superadmin-only), plus GET /api/access-rbac/me (auth-only, returns the caller's role and permission rows so SPAs can derive menu visibility from the same rules that gate the APIs). All shared admin APIs and app-local admin APIs are now enforced by AccessSessionMidware (disabled/must-change-password gate + matrix check). myseliasan gained its own user store (control_user: local stock superadmin + federated myidsan users) with a stock-superadmin bootstrap handoff (POST /api/rbac/users/{id}/elevate retires stock accounts). The parent-to-node reverse command tunnel was also added: a ControlServer on the parent (port pairing.controlPort, default 49533) accepts node-dialed fleet-mTLS WebSocket connections; /api/nodes/{id}/proxy/<node-path> on myseliasan forwards tunneled commands to the node's own API router (node enforces its own auth via synthetic principal); per-node read/write access grants (node_access_grant) gate the proxy. mymatasan received the node-side ControlDispatcher that re-injects parent commands into its own router. Node-pushed events (notifications, going-offline) are ingested into the control plane's unified notification feed.
compatibility: Breaking for the RBAC admin surface: the legacy /api/endpoint-rbac route group and POST /api/sso/authorize are removed; operators must migrate role/permission configuration to /api/access-rbac. The access_role and access_role_permission tables are auto-created by bootstrap on first run. Existing myidsan installs need the superadmin UserRoleId repointed to the new accessrbac superadmin role (done automatically at startup). mymatasan is unaffected (it uses local Basic Auth and opts out of accessrbac). myseliasan requires a new localAuth.username/localAuth.password config block (defaults admin/admin; must change on first login). The pairing.controlPort config key is new and defaults to 49533; no action needed for existing pairings.
